correctness.rationale: The 3x3 mass-normalized Bloch matrix follows directly from Newtonian equations. Strict arrowhead interlacing and F'(lambda)>0 prove exact existence/uniqueness and monotone band. Normalized eigenvector gives dλ/dz=|host|². A sharp elementary minimum of two reciprocal squares yields global slope bound. At coincident resonances the flat middle eigenvalue is uniformly isolated for z in [0,c]; analytic perturbation and explicitly canceled Laurent terms prove a uniform Taylor series and positive coefficient. An independently written symmetric-eigenproblem checker passed 20 sets; they serve only as supporting diagnostics, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The archived mass-in-mass source and the closest multi-resonator source establish forward Bloch bands, exactly flat equal-tuning dark modes, and qualitatively narrow dispersive unequal-tuning bands. The inspected material does not state the uniform quadratic detuning coefficient for arbitrary positive resonator masses or the global nonasymptotic slope/host-share bound. Model-specific vanishing of the linear width term and positivity of the quadratic term are not an immediate bare assertion of the existing forward model. Exact priority remains subject to specialized literature not exhaustively checked.

value.rationale: Two different attached resonator frequencies split the exact zero-group-velocity branch into the slim inter-gap passband observed in multi-resonator devices. The result quantifies the first nonzero bandwidth, with exact coefficient under an arbitrary positive split of local masses; also bounds leakage globally at any detuning by a normalized host-mode participation identity. Such a sharp design tolerance is physically meaningful, is not an arbitrary parameter slice, and concerns a complete two-resonator near-degeneracy in a natural minimal model. It neither claims device-scale transmission nor treats the numerical checker as a source of value.
